Reproduced at the National Archives at Seattle Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Wash., March 29, 1920 Narcisse Martin Cushman School My Friend: I have just received a letter from Mr. Morgan, your Superintendent, who does not think it is best for you to remain home at this time as the whole family has the "flu." Very respectfully, Special Agent in Charge. OHK:MG DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR UNITED STATES INDIAN SERVICE Colville Agency, Nespelem, Wash., March 23, 1920. Mr. C. V. Peel, Special Agent, Cushman Indian School, Tacom, Wash. Dear Mr. Peel: Relative to Mary Martin's request that Narcisse Martin, her son, be permitted to return home to assist her, I will state that I believe it would be very improper for the boy to return home at this time as the whole family has the "flu". I do not know of any special benefit the boy would be to them and it would only mean that there would probably be one more to care for. I will have this matter investigated and should I consider it advisable, I will again write you. Very truly yours, Fred C. Morgan Superintendent. FCM:MG Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Wash., March 19, 1920 Mr. Fred C. Morgan, Supt. Colville Indian Agency Nespelem, Washington Dear Mr. Morgan: Narcisse Martin has received a letter from his mother, Mary Martin, who states that his sister died and that his mother needs him at home. Kindly advise me what action you wish me to take in this matter. Very respectfully, Special Agent in Charge. 5-1142 DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR UNITED STATES INDIAN SERVICE Golville Indian Agency, Nespelem, Wash., Sep. 27, 1919. Supt. E. H. Hammond, Cushman Indian School, Tacoma, Washington. Dear Mr. Hammond: I am enclosing a letter from Narcisse Martin asking me to send him $3.50 of his funds to purchase a suit case and stating that I should be sure not to send the money to you. Thinking that perhaps his plans are to pack up his clothes in the suitcase he contemplates buying and then make his getaway, I do not feel inclined to comply with his request. Perhaps for some reason he may be dissatisfied. So that he can have some money to meet occasional incidental needs I have drawn check #3805, against his account, payable to you, for $30, and enclose the check in this letter. Very truly yours, Fred C. Morgan Superintendent. SJ-Encls. Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Wash., Oct. 3, 1919 Mr. Fred C. Morgan, Supt. Colville Indian Agency Hospalem, Wash. Dear Sir: There is enclosed herewith Official Receipt No. 176077 covering transfer of $30.00 to the account of Narcisse Martin. Very respectfully, Superintendent. /MG Enc. Memo. Solville Agency 5/31/19 No. 1047 ON N. 800 For paid commendation Balance to his credit $300.00 Fred E. Morgan Solville Has been killed Cushman School Tacoma Wash May 29, 1919 Dear Sir, Mr. Morgan please send me a fifteen dollars so my fair to go home here. I left here but dam going to buy clothes from tacoma to go home because we cannot wear a Government things to wear home. So I can buy my own. Your very truly, Your friend, Narcise Martin April 13/919 Cushman Grade School Tacoma Wash. My Dear friend, Say Oh hurry up you send me some money just $25.00 Hatch all I am going home Mr. Hammond said the superintendent I got sour ears my ears is new good I am not good every day I want some money $25.00 I am going home say Mr. Hammond he never likes me I got sour I can hear good I going school long time Mr. Hammond tell me I am just stay here Hatch all you send me some $25.00 say you be sure send me some money $25.00 Hatch all From Narcisse Martin Cushman School Tacoma Wash. Colville Agency, Nespelem, Wash., May 7, 1919. Narcisse Martin, Cushman School, Tacoma, Wash. Dear friend: In accordance with your letter of April 13, 1919 I have transferred $25.00 from your funds at this office to your Superintendent, Mr. Hammond, to be used as your justifiable needs may require. I trust that your ears will improve and that you will be entirely well in a short time. Very truly your friend, (sgd) Fred C Morgan Superintendent RS:DR cc EHH 5-1142 DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR UNITED STATES INDIAN SERVICE Colville Agency, Nespelem, Wash., May 7, 1919. Mr. E. H. I can hearing good. I hat going school every day. Mr. Hammond tell me he tell me you get some money you going home sometimes. I got now money in here. Say Mr. Morgan you send me some money $25.00 Going home Mr. Hammond he said The Superintendent said in here that or write Mr. Fred C. Morgan you get this letters you send me some money write now you get this letters that or write that all from Narcisse Martin Cushman School Tacoma Wash. Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Wn., April 24, 1919 Mr. Fred C. Morgan Colville Agency Nespelem, Wash. My dear Mr. Morgan: I beg to acknowledge receipt of a letter from Narcisse Martin, a pupil of this school, who claims that I said he could go home and ask you for $25.00. Narcisse did have some trouble with an abscess in the ear. His sister has, likewise, suffered from the complaint. Both, however, have improved. Narcisse is in very good health and so far as I can see, there is no reason why he would be returned home. Very respectfully, Superintendent. This form must be executed in duplicate when a child is transferred from a reservation to a nonreservation school. The Superintendent of the nonreservation school will retain the original for his files, and the duplicate shall be deposited in the reservation school records. The reservation superintendent should send to the Commissioner of Indian Affairs his certificate as provided by law. All the blanks must be properly filled in every case. If the information called for on any part of the blank is not known, that fact should be stated. No space should be left unfilled. Whether the parent is living or deceased, the same is given. The person writing the blank referring to the transfer should indicate his relation to the applicant by marking out the word "parent," "guardian," or "next of Kin," having unmarked only the title appropriate to the signer. INDORSEMENTS. The laws relating to the transfer of Indian children from reservations and schools are as follows: That hereafter no Indian child shall be sent from any Indian reservation to a school beyond the State or Territory in which said reservation is situated without the voluntary consent of the father or mother of such child if either of them are living, and if neither of them are living without the voluntary consent of the next of kin of such child. Such consent shall be made before the agent of the reservation, and he shall send to the Commissioner of Indian Affairs his certificate that such consent has been voluntarily given before such child shall be removed from such reservation. And it shall be unlawful for any Indian agent or other employee of the Government to induce, or seek to induce, by withholding rations or by other improper means, the parents or next of kin of any Indian to consent to the removal of any Indian child beyond the limits of any reservation. (28 Stats., p. 906.) Provided, That hereafter no Indian child shall be taken from any school in any State or Territory to a school in any other State against its will or without the written consent of its parents. (29 Stats., p. 348.) That no Indian pupil under the age of fourteen years shall be transported at Government expense to any Indian school beyond the limits of the State or Territory in which the parents of such child reside or of the adjoining State or Territory. (35 Stat. L., 781.) The rules provide that— A pupil who has been regularly enrolled in a nonreservation school must not be taken to any other nonreservation school without the consent of both superintendents and the Commissioner of Indian Affairs, and superintendents will be held to strict accountability for such pupils taken to their schools. An Indian boy or girl 18 years old and over may, without the consent of parents or others, personally sign the application form on its being changed to suit the case; but in all cases where the parents are living they should first be consulted. This form is to be used only in transfers from reservations or Indian schools to nonreservation schools. STATEMENT OF TUITION DUE. May 19 1920 Name of Student...
